rows.verified_citation: C. A. R. Hoare, 'An axiomatic basis for computer programming', Communications of the ACM 12(10):576-580, October 1969. DOI 10.1145/363235.363259 resolves to exactly this record (Crossref + ACM).
rows.statement_match: Abstract (Crossref deposit, also OCR'd from primary scan p.576): 'the elucidation of sets of axioms and rules of inference which can be used in proofs of the properties of computer programs'. Triple definition OCR'd verbatim from p.577 (UMich full-text scan): 'To state the required connection between a precondition (P), a program (Q) and a description of the result of its execution (R), we introduce a new notation: P{Q}R. This may be interpreted "If the assertion P is true before initiation of a program Q, then the assertion R will be true on its completion."' Axiom of assignment (x := E), consequence rules, and composition/iteration rules follow, with termination treated separately -- i.e., a partial-correctness calculus usable for backward propagation of obligations from postcondition to precondition.
rows.drift_notes: Notation drift only: the 1969 paper writes P{Q}R (program inside braces), not the modern {P}S{Q} in the registry row. Semantics claim 'partial-correctness calculus' is accurate (correctness conditional on completion; termination not asserted by the rules).

rows.verified_citation: E. W. Dijkstra, 'Guarded commands, nondeterminacy and formal derivation of programs', Communications of the ACM 18(8):453-457, August 1975. DOI 10.1145/360933.360975 resolves to exactly this record (Crossref + ACM publisher page with abstract and keywords).
rows.statement_match: wp calculus confirmed verbatim from Dijkstra's own EWD418 manuscript of this paper (UTexas EWD archive transcription): 'we shall introduce necessary and sufficient -- i.e. so-called "weakest" -- pre-conditions... we shall use the notation "wp(S, R)", where S denotes a statement list and R some condition on the state of the system, to denote the weakest pre-condition for the initial state of the system such that activation of S is guaranteed to lead to a properly terminating activity leaving the system in a final state satisfying the post-condition R.' Guarded commands: Theorem 1 '(Q and BB) => wp(IF, R)', well-foundedness wdec(S,t), wp(DO,T) termination -- the derivation calculus for verified program construction.
rows.drift_notes: Manuscript title variant EWD418 'Guarded commands, non-determinacy and a calculus for the derivation of programs' vs published CACM title; registry cite matches the published record. ACM publisher page (dl.acm.org 403 to fetcher) abstract obtained earlier confirms identical content; keywords: correctness proof, derivation of programs, program semantics, termination.

rows.verified_citation: Donald E. Knuth, 'A generalization of Dijkstra's algorithm', Information Processing Letters 6(1):1-5, February 1977. DOI 10.1016/0020-0190(77)90002-3 resolves to exactly this record (ScienceDirect: Vol 6, Issue 1, pp 1-5).
rows.statement_match: Mechanism confirmed via publisher page and its citing-article description: 'The grammar problem, a generalization of the single-source shortest-path problem introduced by D. E. Knuth (Inform. Process. Lett. 6(1) (1977), 1-5) is to compute the minimum-cost derivation of a terminal string from each nonterminal of a given context-free grammar.' I.e., shortest-path/DP recursion lifted from graphs to grammar derivations (AND over RHS symbols, OR over productions) -- the claimed DP-over-derivation-graphs mechanism.
rows.drift_notes: Citation string wrong on volume: registry says IPL 8(1); actual is IPL 6(1), Feb 1977, pp 1-5. Title is 'A generalization of Dijkstra's algorithm' (no 'shortest path' in title). 'Semiring-style' and 'AND-OR derivation graphs' are fair glosses, not source terms (full text paywalled; mechanism verified from publisher page + primary-adjacent citing description). Fix volume in registry; no semantic change.

rows.verified_citation: Joshua Goodman, 'Semiring Parsing', Computational Linguistics 25(4):573-605, December 1999. ACL Anthology J99-4004; DOI 10.1162/coli.25.4.573.
rows.statement_match: Abstract extracted verbatim from the ACL Anthology PDF: 'We synthesize work on parsing algorithms, deductive parsing, and the theory of algebra applied to formal languages into a general system for describing parsers. Each parser performs abstract computations using the operations of a semiring. The system allows a single, simple representation to be used for describing parsers that compute recognition, derivation forests, Viterbi, n-best, inside values, and other values, simply by substituting the operations of different semirings. We also show how to use the same representation, interpreted differently, to compute outside values.' Body verbatim: items + inference-rules normal form ('we will use an item [i,A,j]... we will use inference rules'), and 'There are three derivation semirings: the derivation forest semiring, the Viterbi-derivation semiring, and the Viterbi-n-best semiring'. Claimed use 'inside weights over deductive parsing systems' confirmed.
rows.drift_notes: Minor page-range discrepancy: anthology PDF pages 573-606 (last page likely blank/end matter) vs dblp 573-605. Registry URL and venue correct.

rows.verified_citation: The DOI 10.1016/j.scico.2003.12.005 resolves to R. Giegerich, C. Meyer, P. Steffen, 'A discipline of dynamic programming over sequence data', Science of Computer Programming 51(3):215-263, 2004 -- NOT to a paper titled 'Algebraic dynamic programming'.
rows.statement_match: ScienceDirect abstract (verbatim, deposited): the paper establishes the ADP discipline as a decomposition of DP algorithms over sequence data into a grammar part (recurrences) and an algebra part (scoring/evaluation), with a formalization of Bellman's Principle as compositionality condition. Registry's 'evaluation algebras' component confirmed; 'composition of yield morphisms' is the right shape but the literal term was not verifiable from the abstract.
rows.drift_notes: Three drifts: (1) registry title 'Algebraic dynamic programming' is the authors' separate LOPSTR'03 paper (LNCS 3018), not the SCP 2004 article this DOI resolves to; (2) 'Bellman's GAP' is NOT in this source -- it is Sauthoff, Giegerich, Hoener zu Siederdissen's later system (2011+); (3) restate claimed use as: ADP discipline = grammar x evaluation algebra decomposition + Bellman's Principle, per SCP 2004; attribute Bellman's GAP separately if the implementation is meant. Venue/volume/pages/year in registry are correct for the DOI.

rows.verified_citation: P. Cousot and R. Cousot, 'Abstract interpretation: a unified lattice model for static analysis of programs by construction or approximation of fixpoints', POPL 1977, pp. 238-252. DOI 10.1145/512950.512973 resolves to exactly this record (Crossref + authors' page).
rows.statement_match: Confirmed in source (authors' page summary, cross-checked by full-text OCR of the authors' own scan PDF): 'Abstract program properties are modeled by a complete semilattice... Elementary program constructs are locally interpreted by order-preserving functions which are used to associate a system of equations with a program. The program global properties are then defined as one of the extreme fixpoints of that system, Tarski[55]... program properties obtained by an abstract interpretation of a program are consistent with those obtained by a more refined interpretation... limits of finite Kleene[52]'s sequences. Section 9 introduces finite fixpoint approximation methods... shown to be consistent with the abstraction process.' Fixpoint-approximation half of the claimed mechanism fully confirmed.
rows.drift_notes: Galois half is drift: 'Galois' occurs 0 times in the full 1977 paper (15-page OCR of the authors' scan; keywords fixpoint=40, Tarski=7, Kleene=19 prove extraction quality), and 'collecting semantics' as a term also does not appear ('collect*' 0 hits). POPL'77 proves abstraction soundness as a consistency theorem over the semilattice, via an abstraction function; the alpha/gamma Galois-connection formulation appears in the Cousots' POPL 1979 'Systematic design of program analysis frameworks' (its summary: the connection between complete lattices 'is related to Galois connections'). Restate: cite POPL'77 for semilattice + extreme fixpoints + consistency + finite fixpoint approximation; add POPL'79 (or Cousot-Cousot 1992) for the Galois alpha/gamma form.

rows.verified_citation: E. Clarke, O. Grumberg, S. Jha, Y. Lu, S. Veith, 'Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement', CAV 2000, LNCS 1855, pp. 154-169. DOI 10.1007/10722167_15 resolves to exactly this record (Springer).
rows.statement_match: Verbatim from the paper (Technion co-author copy, byte-identical text): 'continues to refine the abstraction function by partitioning equivalence classes until a real counterexample is found, or the ACTL* property is verified. The partitioning procedure is guaranteed to terminate since each equivalence class must contain at least one element. Thus, our method is complete.' Also: 'If a concrete counterexample is found, then the algorithm terminates.' Scope assumption stated by the authors: 'Our methodology is complete for the fragment of ACTL* which has counterexamples that are either paths or loops.' Full abstract matches the Springer chapter page.
rows.drift_notes: Registry claim 'loop termination conditions' accurate, including its stated assumption (ACTL* fragment with path/loop counterexamples). No drift.

rows.verified_citation: T. J. Green, G. Karvounarakis, V. Tannen, 'Provenance semirings', PODS 2007, pp. 31-40. DOI 10.1145/1265530.1265535 resolves to exactly this record (Crossref + ACM).
